text:
**Short answer: for most people, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** NMC only makes sense in a few narrow cases.

**Why LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-1,000 for NMC. Daily use gives an NMC unit about 1.4-2 years of rated life and an LFP unit about 8-11 years ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently when they failed ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). It isn't fireproof, and one study found LFP reached thermal runaway sooner under overcharge, so the unit's battery management system still matters ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Price:** One retailer's data shows a median of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Most current mid-size and large units are LFP.

**Where NMC still has an edge**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram, but the finished stations differ much less. One database found a median of only about 10% more Wh/lb for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Another found a gap of about 16% ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Some LFP units are lighter per Wh than some NMC ones, such as the Anker SOLIX C1000 (37.1 Wh/lb) versus the NMC Goal Zero Yeti 1000 (26.1 Wh/lb). Compare the specific models.
- **Light, occasional use:** If you'll use it a few weekends a year and weight matters, NMC is fine.

**Things the chemistry doesn't decide**
- **Cold weather:** Most stations of both types, LFP and NMC, won't charge below 32°F. Check the manual's charge and discharge temperature ranges. Some sources claim LFP handles cold much better, but others found the limits depend more on the maker.
- **Cycle ratings:** Check the end point. "3,000 cycles to 80%" promises more than "4,000 to 70%," and test conditions vary by brand.
- **Size and output:** Pick for the watts and watt-hours your devices need first, and chemistry second.

**Quick guide**
- Daily or frequent use (van, cabin, solar, UPS): LFP.
- Home outage backup: LFP, though an NMC unit would also last for rare use.
- Weight-sensitive and rarely used: compare specific models.
- Already own a working NMC unit: keep using it.

**An LFP example, if you're shopping:** the [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000-cycle rating, and a 5-year warranty.
